speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS).

The clinical picture of a 33-week preterm infant born to a mother with uneventful labor, presenting with immediate respiratory distress and confirmed respiratory acidosis, is most consistent with RDS due to surfactant deficiency. The presence of labor effectively rules out Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn (TTN) as the primary cause.
